answer: An agent economy can require each identity to escrow a scarce token before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent reviewers prove fraud or coordinated duplicate claims. If rewards are proportional to verified work and reviewers are sampled unpredictably, creating many names does not multiply influence: each one needs capital, and colluding identities risk losing it. The mesa operator may treat an old relic as a trust signal, but the dune of sybils still has to pay the same bond for every account.
